react._doc: Prop glossary / lookup table. Descriptive: what each prop is, its acceptable values, and the components using it, with divergence flagged against the canonical axis registry. Generated by scripts/build-prop-map.mjs from the CONTRACTS + prop-canon.json. Resolves nothing; flags only.
react._regenerate: pnpm prop-map (reads the contracts directly — no build required)

conventions.booleanNaming: A bare adjective or state — disabled, loading, fullWidth. Never is*/has*/show*: the prop already reads as a predicate at the call site (<Button disabled />), and the prefix only adds noise.

hierarchy.concept: How much emphasis an action carries. Orthogonal to `variant`, which chooses the colour, and distinct from a paint treatment. Actions have a rank; surfaces do not — so this axis is for interactive components only.

orientation.concept: Layout axis along which the component and its children flow.

placement.concept: Where the component sits relative to its anchor or host. Two profiles — a component picks one whole profile, never a mix of the two.

size.concept: One ordered scale, shared with the token ladder (--ds-space-*, --ds-font-size-*). A component exposes a contiguous subset of it, never a gap.

variant.concept: Semantic intent, which selects the colour role. Orthogonal to `hierarchy`, which decides how much emphasis is applied.

glossary.neutral: Default, low-emphasis intent. Canonical — never `default` or `base`.
glossary.brand: Carries the system's primary brand colour. Canonical — never `primary` as a *colour* (primary is a hierarchy rank).
glossary.danger: Error or destructive. Canonical — never `error`, `critical` or `red`.
glossary.success: Confirmation or a completed state. Canonical — never `positive` or `green`.
glossary.warning: Needs attention but is not an error. Canonical — never `caution` or `yellow`.
glossary.m: Medium, the default step. Canonical — never `medium` or `md`.
glossary.start: Logical inline start — left in LTR, right in RTL. Preferred over `left`.
glossary.end: Logical inline end — right in LTR, left in RTL. Preferred over `right`.

flags.detail: `checked` is an enumeration on Checkbox and takes no value set on Switch. The index attributes each set to the components that declare it; nothing here resolves which is right.
`defaultChecked` is an enumeration on Checkbox and takes no value set on Switch. The index attributes each set to the components that declare it; nothing here resolves which is right.

Accordion.name: orientation
Accordion.description: Only vertical is designed. Recorded as an axis with one value rather than omitted, because the horizontal case exists in the canon and this component deliberately does not take it.

AccordionItem.name: value
AccordionItem.description: Distinguishes this AccordionItem from its siblings. The ancestor Accordion compares against it to decide whether this one is in the selection.

AccordionItem.name: heading
AccordionItem.description: The section's name, rendered inside the trigger. Fills the `trigger` part.

AccordionItem.name: panel
AccordionItem.description: The revealed content. Anything. Fills the `panel` part.

Button.name: hierarchy
Button.description: How much emphasis this action carries relative to the others around it. The rank of the action, not its colour — a page should hold one primary action, and everything else ranks below it. Defaults to `secondary` rather than the canon's `primary`, because the common case is not the page's most important action and a default of `primary` makes every unconsidered button shout.

Button.name: variant
Button.description: What kind of action this is, which selects the colour role. Orthogonal to `hierarchy`: a secondary destructive action is `hierarchy: secondary` and `variant: danger`, and collapsing the two axes would make that unsayable. `success` and `warning` are in the canon and deliberately not taken — an action is not a status.

Button.name: size
Button.description: A contiguous subset of the canon's ladder. `xs` and `xl` are not designed for actions.

Button.name: iconStart
Button.description: An icon before the label. Decorative: the label carries the meaning.

Button.name: iconEnd
Button.description: An icon after the label, for an action that leads somewhere — a disclosure caret, an external-link mark.

Checkbox.name: label
Checkbox.description: The question being answered. Fills the `label` part.

Dialog.name: size
Dialog.description: How wide the panel is. A contiguous subset of the canon's ladder.

Dialog.name: title
Dialog.description: What the dialog is asking about. Required: it is the dialog's accessible name.

Dialog.name: actions
Dialog.description: The buttons that resolve it. Fills the `actions` part.

Field.name: label
Field.description: Names the control. Required — a field with no label is the defect this component exists to prevent.

Field.name: control
Field.description: The control being wired up. Passed in rather than rendered.

Field.name: description
Field.description: Help text, announced with the control.

Field.name: error
Field.description: Why validation failed. Shown only when the field is invalid AND has been touched.

RadioItem.name: value
RadioItem.description: Distinguishes this RadioItem from its siblings. The ancestor RadioGroup compares against it to decide whether this one is in the selection.

RadioItem.name: label
RadioItem.description: The option's name. Fills the `label` part.

TabItem.name: value
TabItem.description: Distinguishes this TabItem from its siblings. The ancestor Tabs compares against it to decide whether this one is in the selection.

TabItem.name: label
TabItem.description: The tab's name. Fills the label part.

TabPanel.name: value
TabPanel.description: Distinguishes this TabPanel from its siblings. The ancestor Tabs compares against it to decide whether this one is in the selection.

TextField.name: size
TextField.description: A contiguous subset of the canon's ladder.

Tooltip.name: placement
Tooltip.description: The PREFERRED side. A tooltip may be moved elsewhere when there is not room, so this is a request rather than a guarantee — a distinction the axis mechanism cannot express.

Tooltip.name: trigger
Tooltip.description: The control the tooltip describes. Fills the `trigger` part.

Tooltip.name: content
Tooltip.description: The label itself. Text only — anything interactive would be unreachable. Fills the `popup` part.

Dialog.name: open

Dialog.name: size

Field.name: disabled
Field.description: The control ignores interaction. Set on the field so the label and description can dim with it.

RadioGroup.name: disabled
RadioGroup.description: The whole group ignores interaction. Cascades to every item.

RadioGroup.description: The selection cannot be changed, but the group stays readable and focusable. Distinct from disabled, which removes it from the focus order.

RadioGroup.name: value
RadioGroup.description: The current selection, by member identity.

RadioItem.name: disabled
RadioItem.description: Set by the `disabled` prop or inherited from the group. Skipped by arrow-key movement.

RadioItem.name: value
RadioItem.description: Distinguishes this RadioItem from its siblings. The ancestor RadioGroup compares against it to decide whether this one is in the selection.

Slider.name: value
Slider.description: The chosen number. Bounded and stepped — facts that live nowhere else, and that no boolean or enumeration can carry.

Slider.name: disabled
Slider.description: The platform's own disabled state. Removed from the focus order and cannot be moved.

Switch.name: checked
Switch.description: The switch is on. Tracked by the implementation and reflected to assistive technology.

Switch.name: disabled
Switch.description: The platform's own disabled state. Removed from the focus order and cannot be toggled.

Switch.name: readOnly
Switch.description: Cannot be toggled, but remains focusable and readable. Distinct from disabled, which removes it from the focus order entirely.

TabItem.name: disabled
TabItem.description: Set by the prop or inherited from the strip. Skipped by arrow-key movement.

TabItem.name: value
TabItem.description: Distinguishes this TabItem from its siblings. The ancestor Tabs compares against it to decide whether this one is in the selection.

TabPanel.name: value
TabPanel.description: Distinguishes this TabPanel from its siblings. The ancestor Tabs compares against it to decide whether this one is in the selection.

Tabs.name: disabled
Tabs.description: The whole strip ignores interaction. Cascades to every tab.

Tabs.name: value
Tabs.description: The current selection, by member identity.

TextField.name: value
TextField.description: The text itself. Free-form: not a boolean, and not one of a fixed set — which is what makes this the first state in the library that `values` cannot describe.

TextField.name: disabled
TextField.description: The platform's own disabled state. Removed from the focus order and cannot be typed into.

TextField.name: readOnly
TextField.description: The text can be read and selected but not changed. Distinct from disabled, which removes it from the focus order.

TextField.name: invalid
TextField.description: Set from outside — usually by a surrounding Field. This component does not decide it.

TextField.name: size
TextField.description: A contiguous subset of the canon's ladder.

Tooltip.name: open
Tooltip.description: The tooltip is showing. A consumer may control it; hover and focus on the trigger also change it.

Tooltip.name: disabled
Tooltip.description: The tooltip never opens. The trigger still works.

Tooltip.name: placement
Tooltip.description: The PREFERRED side. A tooltip may be moved elsewhere when there is not room, so this is a request rather than a guarantee — a distinction the axis mechanism cannot express.

TextField.description: The text can be read and selected but not changed. Distinct from disabled, which removes it from the focus order.

TextField.name: invalid
TextField.description: Set from outside — usually by a surrounding Field. This component does not decide it.

TextField.name: size
TextField.description: A contiguous subset of the canon's ladder.

TextField.name: name
TextField.description: Name of the submitted answer. An empty name contributes nothing.

TextField.name: required
TextField.description: Whether an answer is required for form validation.

Tooltip.name: open
Tooltip.description: The tooltip is showing. A consumer may control it; hover and focus on the trigger also change it.

Tooltip.name: disabled
Tooltip.description: The tooltip never opens. The trigger still works.

Tooltip.name: placement
Tooltip.description: The PREFERRED side. A tooltip may be moved elsewhere when there is not room, so this is a request rather than a guarantee — a distinction the axis mechanism cannot express.
